caption:
In Bengaluru and Gurugram boardrooms, the sharpest person in the room is often the one who speaks last — and only after someone else has said their idea for them.

That hesitation gets diagnosed as an English problem. It isn't. Vocabulary was never the issue. Delivery was.

Pace. Pause. Posture. The discipline of holding the floor without raising your voice. A command voice is built from bearing, not grammar — and bearing translates into every language you speak.

Business Today's Big Story on India Inc warming to non-English-speaking executives, and BW People's "Confidence Has A Mother Tongue," are both pointing at the same thing from the outside. Here is the inside view: fluency courses fix your sentences. They do not fix your stance.

Colonel Suhag spent 35 years in command, where orders had to land the first time. The Lumina Method teaches the same mechanics for the room you're in on Monday.

topic.title: English fluency isn't competence — reframe it as bearing
topic.angle: Competent regional-language-first managers in Bengaluru and Gurugram boardrooms aren't short of ideas, they're second-guessing their first sentence, and Lumina can reframe this as a delivery problem — pace, pause, posture, holding the floor — that works in any language rather than a vocabulary problem to be fixed with fluency courses.
